claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder.
The powder has particle-size distribution and chemical homogeneity suitable for LPBF processing.
The intervention uses a chessboard scanning strategy with short, overlapping scan vectors and interleaved scan directions.
Track overlap and dwell time are to be optimized through a controlled parametric study.
The proposed scan strategy will produce a uniformly refined microstructure.
The proposed scan strategy will minimize thermal gradients and local cooling-rate disparities.
Reduced thermal gradients and cooling-rate disparities will limit microsegregation.
Reduced thermal gradients and cooling-rate disparities will reduce residual-stress buildup.
The chessboard scanning pattern redistributes laser energy more evenly across the build area.
Overlapping laser exposure and controlled dwell times cause localized reheating.
Localized reheating homogenizes melt-pool solidification.
More homogeneous melt-pool solidification reduces compositional segregation, residual thermal stress, and resulting defects.
Relative to standard LPBF scanning, the optimized strategy will directionally reduce residual thermal stress.
Relative to standard LPBF scanning, the optimized strategy will reduce microsegregation.
Relative to standard LPBF scanning, the optimized strategy will reduce process-induced defect density.
Reduced stress, segregation, and defects will improve tensile, ductility, or fatigue performance.
Conventionally scanned LPBF AlCrFeNiSi parts typically have notable residual stress, segregation, and comparatively high defect density.
The proposed intervention is expected to apply to small-to-moderately complex parts processed under typical LPBF conditions.
Applicability to highly complex or non-standard geometries has not been established.
X-ray diffraction, SEM-EDS, computed tomography, tensile testing, and fatigue testing can provide measurable comparisons of the proposed outcomes.
